results_title: Pages found (also streaming live into Proxy History)
empty_description: Set a start URL above and click Start crawl.
guide_intro: Starts at a URL and follows every same-site link it finds, mapping out the site; Burp/ZAP call this a "spider". Every page it fetches is saved into Proxy History live, exactly like intercepted traffic, ready to send to Repeater, Intruder, or the scanners.
guide_step1_title: Set a start URL and limits
guide_step1_body: <0>Max depth</0> is how many link-hops away from the start page it'll follow. <1>Max pages</1> is a hard cap on the total pages fetched: both exist so a crawl can't run away on a huge site. "Include subdomains" widens scope from just the exact host to anything under it.
guide_step2_body: Controls how many pages it fetches at once. <0>Cautious</0> is gentler on the target; <1>Fast</1> finishes quicker at the cost of more concurrent load.
guide_step3_title: Click "Start crawl" and watch it stream in
guide_step3_body: New pages land in the table (and in Proxy History) as they're fetched. Each row shows the page's title, how many hops deep it is, how many links it had, and how many forms were found on it. "Stop" cancels a running crawl at any point.
guide_step4_body: Every <0><form></0> found gets its action URL, method, and input field names recorded: a quick map of every place the site accepts input, worth feeding into the SQL Injection or XSS scanners next.
guide_footer_note: This deliberately ignores <0>robots.txt</0>: that file is a convention for search engines, not a security boundary, and a pentest spider exists to find what a polite crawler wouldn't. It does make a real request per page found, though, so only point it at hosts you're authorized to test.
